items.grounds: Re-derived both ways. The layout fact is true in the staged WEB map: a paragraph opens at web:Isa.24.1, the next at web:Isa.24.14, none between and 0 continuation-paragraph folds inside web:Isa.24.1-13. But tier-4 layout is never boundary evidence, as driver or as corroboration (only the tier-3 parashah layer carries a corroboration role), and this rationale puts the paragraph block to consistent-with work at the row's one point of external support. At the Isa.24.13|Isa.24.14 seam nothing else external re-derives: the parashah inventory's nearest segs are PE at oshb:Isa.23.18 (single-witness) and SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.24.15 (single-witness), no seg at the seam; the staged device inventory carries 0 ch-24 sites for verse-initial massa headers, hoy onsets, koh-amar, postpositive neum signatures, and amar-or-vayomer-plus-YHWH adjacency; the chapter's sole day-formula site is oshb:Isa.24.21 (day-formula substring, skeleton tier — sweep: 45 verses book-wide, exactly 1 in this chapter); and the seam itself is a subject shift inside continuous third person, כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת (oshb:Isa.24.13, byte tier) against הֵ֛מָּה יִשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם יָרֹ֑נּוּ (oshb:Isa.24.14, byte tier), neither side carrying an addressee. A tier-4 fact doing corroboration work in the boundary_rationale of a high-confidence row is a defective warrant element, though not alone load-bearing: confirmed at the filed severity.

Re-swept both count objects. The six-word splice כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.24.3, byte tier) stands at exactly 1 verse at byte tier, 1 at accent_stripped, and 1 at skeleton (sweep: 1 verse at each tier, Isa.24.3 alone), so it has no twin at oshb:Isa.22.25 at any staged tier — that verse ends on the short formula כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר (oshb:Isa.22.25, byte tier) with no object phrase following. The 4-verse digit re-derives only against the short formula as its own count object: the skeleton-tier phrase sweep of that formula returns exactly 4 verses (Isa.1.2, Isa.22.25, Isa.24.3, Isa.25.8), and its 22.25-vs-24.3 pairing is indeed skeleton-only, the verb differing in vowels between the sites. The shipped parenthetical attaches the twin claim and the digit to the six-word splice, while the object actually swept is never spliced anywhere in the row; and oshb:Isa.25.8 is the closing verse of a sibling row of this same part, ending byte-identical כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר (oshb:Isa.25.8, byte tier), so 'elsewhere in the book' is not a neutral description of the recurrence set. Defective count-object and tier attachment inside a texture note that carries no boundary: confirmed at the filed severity.

Re-derived at the row's own bytes. oshb:Isa.24.14 opens הֵ֛מָּה יִשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם יָרֹ֑נּוּ (oshb:Isa.24.14, byte tier), a third-person report — “These shall lift up their voice. They will shout for the majesty of Yahweh.” (web:Isa.24.14) — but the row's closing verse pivots to direct address: כַּבְּד֣וּ יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.24.15, byte tier), a plural imperative by its initial-syllable pointing (no morphology layer is staged; the form is argued from the pointed bytes and both witnesses' renderings), “Therefore glorify Yahweh in the east” (web:Isa.24.15), WEB closing the verse on an exclamation. So the sentence 'narrated wholly in the third person through Isa.24.15, with no addressee or scene change of its own inside the two verses' is byte-false: 24.15 addresses an audience where 24.14 has none. The row's own boundary_rationale ('the summons continues as an imperative call') and its hymn.praise_summons_imperative signal assert the contrary fact, and the false sentence is the one device_notes itself names 'the warrant that survives' the disclosed cross-seam anaphora onto כְּנֹ֣קֶף זַ֔יִת (oshb:Isa.24.13, byte tier) — the load-bearing defense of this row's opening seam under the cross-seam cohesion law. Byte-false load-bearing warrant: confirmed at the filed severity.

Re-derived inside the row's final verse. The sole athnach of oshb:Isa.25.5 falls on תַּכְנִ֑יעַ (oshb:Isa.25.5, byte tier), the fifth of the verse's eleven tokens, and the verse closes זְמִ֥יר עָֽרִיצִ֖ים יַעֲנֶֽה (oshb:Isa.25.5, byte tier) — a third-person close, “the song of the dreaded ones will be brought low” (web:Isa.25.5). The warrant's 'continues through Isa.25.5, closing on a second-person verb' therefore misstates the verse's own close, and the intra-verse register turn at the athnach is disclosed nowhere in the row. The closing edge survives on grounds the row already ships: וְעָשָׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת (oshb:Isa.25.6, byte tier) opening the next verse with an explicit third-person divine subject, plus the PE seg after oshb:Isa.25.5 (parashah inventory, single-witness, tier-3 non-driving) — so the defective leg is not alone load-bearing. The calibration leg re-verifies against owner law: the owner-ruled book strategy registers the 24-27 cycle's song insets, 25:1-5 among them, as an expected low-confidence region for exactly this voice alternation, yet the row ships confidence high with frontier_flag_considered false. Defective warrant plus disclosure and calibration shortfall, short of load-bearing: confirmed at the filed severity.

Re-derived on both sides of the Isa.26.6|Isa.26.7 seam. The row's last two verses are third-person description of God's act: כִּ֤י הֵשַׁח֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י מָר֔וֹם (oshb:Isa.26.5, byte tier) with יַשְׁפִּילֶ֤נָּה יַשְׁפִּילָהּ֙ (oshb:Isa.26.5, byte tier), then תִּרְמְסֶ֖נָּה רָ֑גֶל (oshb:Isa.26.6, byte tier), “The foot shall tread it down” (web:Isa.26.6). Inside the span, second-person address to Yahweh stands exactly once, תִּצֹּ֖ר שָׁל֣וֹם שָׁל֑וֹם כִּ֥י בְךָ֖ בָּטֽוּחַ (oshb:Isa.26.3, byte tier): 26.1 is third person, פִּתְח֖וּ שְׁעָרִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.26.2, byte tier) and בִּטְח֥וּ בַֽיהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.26.4, byte tier) are imperatives to human addressees with Yahweh in third-person reference, and 26.5-26.6 are third person. Past the seam the second-person register to Yahweh resumes at once: after the nominal colon אֹ֥רַח לַצַּדִּ֖יק מֵֽישָׁרִ֑ים (oshb:Isa.26.7, byte tier), the same verse turns to יָשָׁ֕ר מַעְגַּ֥ל צַדִּ֖יק תְּפַלֵּֽס (oshb:Isa.26.7, byte tier), “You who are upright make the path of the righteous level.” (web:Isa.26.7), then אַ֣ף אֹ֧רַח מִשְׁפָּטֶ֛יךָ יְהוָ֖ה קִוִּינ֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.26.8, byte tier) with the divine name vocative. The stated closing-edge driver — a turn from the song's second-person address of Yahweh to a third-person maxim — is byte-false in direction on both sides of the seam, and it recurs verbatim in strongest_rejected_alternative; only the gnomic nominal register of 26.7's first colon survives in the bytes. Byte-false load-bearing closing-edge warrant: confirmed at the filed severity.

Re-verified all three legs. The WEB punctuation fact is exact in the staged text: one opening quotation mark in web:Isa.26.1, one closing in web:Isa.26.6, 0 quotation-punctuation instances across web:Isa.26.2-26.5 and across web:Isa.26.7 through web:Isa.27.1, resuming only at web:Isa.27.2. The parashah inventory marks nothing at the Isa.26.6|Isa.26.7 seam — the ch-26 segs are SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.26.10, oshb:Isa.26.11, oshb:Isa.26.19, and oshb:Isa.26.21 (single-witness), the nearest to the seam in either direction being SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.26.10 (the preceding seg falls after oshb:Isa.25.12) — and absence is never counterevidence. Translation punctuation is tier-4 and never boundary evidence, as driver or as corroboration, yet the row carries it in boundary_rationale as corroboration of the edge and restates it in strongest_rejected_alternative, dressed with a digit that gives it the outward form of a sweep, while shipping confidence high with frontier_flag_considered false inside the 26:1-6 song inset the owner-ruled strategy registers as an expected low-confidence region. With the companion finding's person-shift warrant byte-false, the tier-4 fact stands beside only the byte-true gnomic-register observation at the seam. Defective tier-4 corroboration in two fields, not alone load-bearing: confirmed at the filed severity.

Re-swept all three count objects. לִפְקֹ֛ד (oshb:Isa.26.21, byte tier) sweeps at whole-token skeleton to exactly 1 verse (Isa.26.21); יִפְקֹ֣ד (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) sweeps at whole-token skeleton to 5 verses (Isa.23.17, Isa.24.21, Isa.24.22, Isa.27.1, Isa.27.3). The two hit sets are disjoint, so the shipped sentence's 'agree only at the consonantal skeleton' is false as written — there is no whole-token skeleton the two forms share. The 18-verse digit belongs to the bare three-consonant root substring as its own count object (sweep: 18 verses book-wide at skeleton-substring tier), which is exactly how the row on the far side of the same seam states the same device ('links only at the shared three-consonant root, not at byte tier or at the whole-token skeleton'), leaving the seam-pair describing one cross-seam echo incompatibly. The echo is disclosed in the shipped note as not binding the two rows into one unit, so the conflation is a tier and count-object defect in texture rather than a boundary carrier: confirmed at the filed severity.
